label: dsa-mid-wrong-complexity
questions:
Title: Two Sum
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Each input has exactly one solution and you may not use the same element twice.
Example 1: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9, output [0, 1], because 2 + 7 = 9.
Constraints: 2 <= nums.length <= 10^4, -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9.

Title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
Example 1: s = abcabcbb, output 3, because abc is the longest.
Constraints: 0 <= s.length <= 5 * 10^4.

turns.content: Hi! Let's start with problem one, Two Sum. It's on your screen now. Any clarifying questions?
Yeah, can the array have negative numbers, and is there always exactly one answer?
Yes, negatives are allowed, and there's always exactly one answer. What's your approach?

So the brute force is checking every pair, that's O of n squared. Better is a hash map. I walk the array once, and for each number I check if target minus that number is already in the map. If it is I return both indices, otherwise I store the number with its index. That's O of n time.
Space is O of one, because we only keep the one dictionary.
Okay. Go ahead and code it.
Done. I enumerate, check the complement first so I don't use the same element twice, then store it. I return an empty list if nothing is found, though the problem says that won't happen.
First 3, complement 3 isn't in the map, so I store 3 at index 0. Second 3, complement 3 is in the map at index 0, so I return 0 and 1. Correct.
Nice. Let's move to problem two, the longest substring without repeating characters.
Okay, I'll start each index, grow a set until I hit a repeat, and track the best length. Let me write it.

It's O of n squared in the worst case because of the nested loops. I know there's a sliding window that makes it O of n, where you move the left pointer past the repeated character, but I'd need a minute to get the pointer updates right.
That's fine, we're at time. Thanks, that's the interview.
